issues.description: changedFiles as mutable instance state complects time, identity, and value on the provider
issues.detail: The provider now carries a mutable `changedFiles` field plus a `globCache` that must be invalidated whenever it changes. That is place-oriented programming: one identity, two values across time, with `isIncluded` silently behaving differently before and after `onTestRunStart`. Pass the changed-file set as a value into the functions that need it, or compute a fresh inclusion predicate per run, instead of mutating provider state and clearing caches by hand.

issues.description: isIncluded conflates glob membership with changed-set membership in one boolean
issues.detail: `isIncluded` originally answered one question: does this filename match include/exclude globs. It now also answers "is it in the changed set," caches the conjunction, and depends on call ordering relative to `onTestRunStart`. Two concerns are complected into one cached predicate. Keep `isIncluded` as a pure include/exclude check and compose a separate `isChanged` filter at the call sites that actually care.

issues.description: Lifecycle hook onTestRunStart added in three call sites by hand instead of as data
issues.detail: Three separate `await this.coverageProvider?.onTestRunStart?.()` calls were sprinkled across `core.ts`. That is the kind of incidental complexity that grows: the next lifecycle event will need three more edits, and one will be forgotten. The run lifecycle should be expressed as a single sequence of phases the provider participates in, not as ad-hoc calls bolted onto each entry point.

issues.description: cleanUrl added to isIncluded silently changes the meaning of cached keys
issues.detail: Switching the cache key from `slash(_filename)` to `slash(cleanUrl(_filename))` changes the identity of every entry in `globCache` and the contract of `isIncluded` for callers that pass query-suffixed paths. This is bundled into a feature PR with no isolated test or comment explaining why query params now belong in coverage inclusion. Either land it as its own change with a focused test, or document the invariant being established.

issues.description: transform function for CLI flag uses string sentinels instead of a typed value
issues.detail: The CLI transform compares against the strings `'true'`, `'yes'`, `'false'`, `'no'` and also the booleans `true`/`false`, returning a `boolean | string` union downstream. That is easy-not-simple: the parser is doing both coercion and pass-through, and the resulting type forces every consumer to re-discriminate. A small parsed value type (`{ kind: 'off' } | { kind: 'on' } | { kind: 'ref'; ref: string }`) would separate parsing from interpretation cleanly.

issues.description: Inheritance rule from test.changed to coverage.changed is implicit and untyped
issues.detail: `if (resolved.coverage.changed === undefined && resolved.changed !== undefined)` quietly couples two independent options at resolution time, and a user who passes `coverage: { changed: false }` is distinguished from `undefined` only by JS truthiness. The inheritance is real product behavior and deserves to be expressed as a named function returning the resolved coverage-changed value, with `undefined` vs `false` semantics documented at the boundary rather than buried in `resolveConfig`.

review.summary: The feature is useful and the tests are honest, but the implementation complects several concerns that were separable. `BaseCoverageProvider` grows a mutable `changedFiles` field plus a cache that must be hand-invalidated, `isIncluded` now answers two questions instead of one, and a new lifecycle hook is wired by hand at three call sites. Pulling the changed-file set out as a value passed into pure inclusion functions, and expressing the run lifecycle and CLI parsing as data, would keep the same behavior with markedly less place-oriented state. None of this is a blocker, but the easy path here is not the simple one.
